title: ～かもしれない — “might ～ / maybe ～”
summary: かもしれない says that something is possible, but the speaker is not sure. It attaches to the plain form of verbs and adjectives, and to nouns and na-adjectives without だ. Politely, it is かもしれません.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞の普通形 ＋ かもしれない
patterns.gloss: 降る → 降るかもしれない / 帰った → 帰ったかもしれない

patterns.form: 名詞・な形容詞（だ を除く）＋ かもしれない
patterns.gloss: 雨かもしれない / 間違いかもしれない

body.p: It combines かも and しれない (“cannot know”), originally meaning “I can't tell whether it is so.” From that came the sense “it is possible.” In speech, かも alone is common.
Use it to make a modest guess about things you are unsure of, such as weather or other people's actions: 午後から雨が降るかもしれません. The chance may be about half or even low.
はずだ and きっと show strong confidence; かもしれない shows low confidence and offers one possibility among others. でしょう is the speaker's guess, while かもしれない signals that other possibilities remain.

examples.ja: 午後（ごご）から雨（あめ）が降（ふ）るかもしれません。
examples.romaji: Gogo kara ame ga furu kamo shiremasen.
examples.tr: It might rain in the afternoon.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）はもう家（いえ）に帰（かえ）ったかもしれない。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mō ie ni kaetta kamo shirenai.
examples.tr: He might have already gone home.
examples.note: The past plain form (帰った) refers to something that may already have happened.

examples.ja: この道（みち）は間違（まちが）っているかもしれません。
examples.romaji: Kono michi wa machigatte iru kamo shiremasen.
examples.tr: This road might be the wrong one.

pitfalls: Do not use だ before it: 雨かもしれない, not 雨だかもしれない.
Do not use it for things you are sure of; use はずだ or にちがいない.
